title: How many rooms and diamonds did the king's daughters have?
description: The story of the king's three daughters, their baskets, keys, rooms, tables, necklaces and diamonds is followed level by level to count the rooms and the diamonds. Keeko's doubt is that seven levels of three give three times seven diamonds.
teaching_notes: One idea: when every level multiplies the count by three, the total is a power of three, and powers with the same base can be joined. Watch for students who add seven threes instead of multiplying them.

source: In the story, find the number of rooms and the number of dia
video_script.why: The child can write repeated multiplication as a power and now follows a story where every level is three times the one before.
video_script.substitution: The book's own story of the king's three daughters, with the rooms and the diamonds counted level by level.
video_script.anchor: a tree of the story on the board, from the king down through daughters, baskets, keys, rooms, tables, necklaces and diamonds
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks seven levels of three give three times seven, which is twenty one diamonds. Every level multiplies by three, so the threes are multiplied together, not added.
video_script.payoff_line: In all, there are eighty one rooms and two thousand one hundred eighty seven diamonds

final_answer.spoken: eighty one rooms and two thousand one hundred eighty seven diamonds

maths_rules: slip: 3 × 7 = 21 adds seven threes, it does not multiply them
video_script.design: One idea: every level multiplies by three, so the total is a power of three. The tree stays on the board all video; the last multiplication is left open until the answer; one slip at the end.

<bookmark mark='nine'/>Three daughters have three times three baskets, which is nine.
<bookmark mark='keys'/>Nine baskets have twenty seven keys.
<bookmark mark='rooms'/>Twenty seven keys open eighty one rooms.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, count the diamonds in one room.
Three tables, three necklaces on each, and three diamonds on each necklace.
<bookmark mark='room'/>That is three times three times three, which is twenty seven.

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, the rooms are four threes multiplied, and one room's diamonds are three threes.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Together that is seven threes multiplied, so the diamonds are three to the power seven.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Eighty one times twenty seven is left to find.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>In all, there are eighty one rooms and two thousand one hundred eighty seven diamonds.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The diamonds are eighty one times twenty seven.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks there are seven levels of three, so three times seven makes twenty one diamonds.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>But three times seven only adds seven threes together.
The baskets alone are already nine.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Each level multiplies by three, so the threes are multiplied, not added.
